match.reason: None of the bank points cover saving energy in the home through efficient appliances, insulation, shading or window placement; they teach general energy transfer, transformation and conservation ideas, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Saving energy at home
card: An efficient appliance does the same job using less energy. It wastes less as heat or light that is not needed.
Insulation in ceilings and walls slows the movement of heat. It keeps heat inside in winter and outside in summer, so heaters and coolers run less.
Awnings, blinds and trees shade windows from the summer sun. Windows facing the sun can let in warmth in winter, which cuts heating.
What helps most depends on the season and the climate. A cold place gains most from insulation and winter sun. A hot place gains most from shade and cooling.
draft.remember: Efficient appliances, insulation, shading and window placement cut energy use, and the best choice depends on season and climate.

a.q: How does insulation in a ceiling help a home use less energy?
opts: It slows heat moving through the ceiling
It makes the heater produce more heat
It lets more sunlight in through the roof
It makes lights use less electricity
a.why: Insulation slows heat moving in or out, so heaters and coolers run less. It does not change how much heat a heater makes, and it has no effect on lights.
a.clue: Think about what insulation does to the movement of heat.

b.q: Priya lives in a hot part of Mildura. Her west-facing windows get strong afternoon sun in summer. Which change would most likely cut her energy use in summer?
opts: Adding external shading over the west windows
Adding more windows on the west wall
Taking down the curtains to let in light
Turning on the heater to balance the heat
b.why: Shading stops the summer sun heating the rooms, so the cooler runs less. More west windows would let in more heat. Letting in sun suits winter in a cold place, not a hot summer.
b.clue: In a hot season, the aim is to keep heat out.

a.best: It slows heat moving through the ceiling

b.best: Adding external shading over the west windows
